chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him): When Masqalah ibn Hubayrah al-Shaybani fled to Mu'awiya,
for he had purchased the captives of Banu Najiyah from an agent of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and freed them,
when he (peace be upon him) demanded the money from him, he cheated him and fled to Syria.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful), a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الشَّام: Syria, the region where Mu'awiya was based
key_terms.الشَّيْبَانِيُّ: Al-Shaybani, referring to his tribal affiliation
key_terms.بَنِي نَاجِيَةَ: Banu Najiyah, a specific tribe or family group
key_terms.خَاسَ بِهِ: He cheated him or defrauded him
key_terms.مَصْقَلَةُ بْنُ هُبَيْرَةَ: Masqalah ibn Hubayrah, a companion who defected to Mu'awiya

ai.seo_question: Who was Masqalah ibn Hubayrah and why did he flee to Mu'awiya?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the economic dimensions of Imam Ali’s governance, where he reclaimed the purchase price of freed captives to maintain fiscal justice, illustrating the practical application of property rights in early Islamic society. Masqala’s subsequent defection to Mu'awiya underscores the political fragility of the period, as financial disputes often served as catalysts for tribal allegiances shifting between the Imam and the Umayyad opposition.
